objective: Throttling and rate limits in DynamoDB, Amazon RDS, and Kinesis, and how to work within them
secondaryObjectives: Configuring Lambda functions for the concurrency and performance a pipeline needs

Reduce the frequency of requests using Error retries and exponential backoff', OK to retry; for BatchWriteItem, failed puts come back in UnprocessedItems, 'The most likely cause of a failed read or a failed write is throttling', 'If you retry the batch operation immediately, the underlying read or write requests can still fail due to throttling ... we strongly recommend that you use an exponential backoff algorithm'.

brief.situation: You are the data engineer at Brightmoor Markets, a fictional grocer. At 10:30 you started a backfill that copies five years of loyalty history into the DynamoDB table members (provisioned, 4,000 write capacity units). The checkout app writes points to the same table. Since 10:50 some checkouts fail to add points, and lunch traffic doubles at 12:00.
handover: The backfill is a Lambda, member-backfill, fanned out by a Step Functions Map state with 64 parallel workers; each worker re-sends UnprocessedItems at once, in a loop.
Auto scaling on members tops out at 4,000 write units by design (the budget owner's cap).
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the backfill workers, the checkout app and the table's write capacity.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why checkout was throttled, what you changed, and how the backfill will finish without repeating it.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the saturation to the bulk writer's retries.
parts.modelAnswer: members has 4,000 write units shared by checkout and the backfill. The backfill's 64 workers re-sent UnprocessedItems at once, so it kept the table at 100% and checkout's PutItems were throttled.

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Caps the bulk writer instead of feeding it.
parts.modelAnswer: Restarted the backfill from its checkpoint at 8 workers, 1,500 write units and exponential backoff; checkout's throttling stopped. More workers would have throttled checkout harder, and memory was not the limit.

parts.label: Finish
parts.criteria: Moves bulk work to a quiet time and watches for a repeat.
parts.modelAnswer: The rest runs at 01:00 at the same cap, and an alarm on WriteThrottleEvents pages us if the table is saturated again.

expertPath.text: Consumed 4,000 of 4,000; throttles since 10:47; 64 workers resending at once; backfill 88% of writes.
Restart at 8 workers, 1,500 WCU, backoff; schedule the rest for 01:00 with a throttle alarm.

throttledHarder.headline: Faster is the wrong direction
throttledHarder.body: A table's write capacity is shared. A bulk job that saturates it takes capacity from every other writer; more workers and instant retries only make it worse.

lunchFailed.headline: The live app lost the capacity race
lunchFailed.body: Cap the bulk writer's rate and give it exponential backoff, so the live application keeps the capacity it needs.

shared.headline: Good: working within the limit
shared.body: You saw the capacity was full and the backfill's instant retries were the cause, capped its rate with backoff instead of adding workers, checked checkout, and moved the bulk of the work to a quiet hour with an alarm.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Checkout and the backfill share 4,000 write units. The backfill's 64 workers re-send unprocessed items immediately, so they keep the table saturated and checkout is throttled. Work within the limit: cap the backfill's rate and concurrency and give its retries exponential backoff, then move the bulk of it to a quiet hour with an alarm on throttling. More workers make it worse and Lambda memory is not the bottleneck.
